research.title: Drone-Megaddon
research.subtitle: A Real-Time Strategy Interface for Managing Drone Swarms
research.summary: I co-built an end-to-end Android, radio, and embedded-control prototype that translated real-time strategy interactions into drone commands. The 2014 work established the command interface and execution path; Drone-Megaddon 2026 extends that foundation with a proposed language-and-vision architecture for operator-supervised coordination.

research.title: Drone-Megaddon 2026
research.subtitle: Co-Intelligent Swarm Control with Language and Vision Models
research.summary: I coauthored a proposed extension of our built 2014 drone-control prototype: translate operator language into checked commands, ground references in video and track targets, then coordinate assignments across drones. The architecture places language and vision models inside an operator-supervised system, with explicit choices about edge versus cloud execution, latency, bandwidth, and degraded connectivity. An illustrative search-and-rescue trace shows how the layers work together; the paper reports no quantitative results from a deployed 2026 system.

claim.value: Drone-Megaddon 2026: Co-Intelligent Swarm Control with Language and Vision Models

research.title: Who Trains the Next Senior?
research.subtitle: Managing Software Engineering When AI Makes Code Cheap
research.summary: I coauthored a framework for leading engineering organizations when AI makes code abundant but verification and judgment remain scarce. It connects review theater, engineer development, and team incentives to practical changes: smaller reviewable units, scrutiny matched to consequence, evidence-backed gates, and outcome-based metrics. An exploratory, correlational analysis of several thousand commits from a single organization illustrates why raw activity can overstate progress; the paper turns those observations into testable propositions about verification and apprenticeship.

research.title: A Multi-Layer Framework for Evaluating the Return on Investment of AI Projects
research.authors: Sairam Krishnan, Sonia Gandhi, Andrea Hepp
research.summary: I coauthored a decision framework connecting AI strategy to investment and execution: assess organizational readiness, trace business value through ROIC, phase investment through evidence-based gates, and synthesize a decision scorecard. An eight-category risk assessment makes inference economics, vendor dependency, and organizational friction explicit. Eight illustrative public-company cases, from Salesforce and Spotify to JPMorgan and NatWest, show how the framework changes investment conditions across deployment types; this is illustrative validation, not empirical validation. The work was a Wharton independent study sponsored by Professor Gad Allon.

claim.value: A Multi-Layer Framework for Evaluating the ROI of AI Projects

ventures.name: Ondoway
ventures.thesis: A travel companion that adapts as you walk.
ventures.problem: A useful tour must connect accurate stories with personal interests, walking constraints, and the time a traveler actually has.
ventures.role: Co-founder & CTO. I lead technical strategy, AI architecture, and end-to-end engineering within the founding team.
ventures.system: Graph-grounded storytelling, deterministic itinerary planning, GPS-triggered narration, and calibrated LLM judges against frozen human labels. I trace model and prompt versions, evidence, tokens, latency, and costs—including failed attempts.
ventures.state: Private beta with early testers, including Wharton Executive MBA peers, and initial city support for New York City and Paris. Flutter app, FastAPI backend, and Neo4j graph.
ventures.lesson: I rejected a cheaper factual judge after calibration exposed false rejections of legitimate paraphrases, separating model-quality failures from truncation before making the cost decision.

ventures.name: Persuaider
ventures.thesis: Practice, simulate, and evaluate the hard conversation.
ventures.problem: Negotiation practice needs credible competing interests and feedback grounded in what was actually said and agreed.
ventures.role: Creator & AI Engineering Lead. I built the product, agent behavior, multiagent simulation, and evaluation systems.
ventures.system: Role-conditioned agents with private objectives; stateful AI-versus-AI simulations; LLM deal extraction followed by deterministic utility, walk-away, and value-left-on-the-table calculations; configurable weighted coaching rubrics.
ventures.state: Working interactive practice and autonomous simulations with persisted transcripts and usage. Coaching quotations and numerical references are checked in code, returned for bounded repair, and withheld if validation still fails.
ventures.lesson: I evaluate negotiation economics separately from conversational skill, and require the coaching to point back to its evidence.

ventures.name: Gestiq
ventures.thesis: Deliberate desktop actions from hand motion.
ventures.problem: Camera input is uncertain; useful gesture control must distinguish an intentional action from jitter, tracking loss, and return motion.
ventures.role: Creator. I designed and built the native macOS product, extending my CMU hand-controlled 2048 capstone.
ventures.system: On-device Apple Vision hand-pose estimation, palm-normalized temporal recognition, two-hand controls, and application- and website-aware command routing. Latest-frame processing, target revalidation, and live diagnostics connect perception to guarded actions.
ventures.state: Working macOS application with a SwiftUI interface, menu-bar controls, and local camera processing without uploading video.
ventures.lesson: I carry confidence, timing, and target identity through the whole perception-to-action path, including the final dispatch check.

claim.value: Gestiq: on-device computer vision and contextual gesture control

ventures.name: Lore / DependIQ
ventures.thesis: The verification layer AI coding agents lack.
ventures.problem: Repository-local tooling cannot explain the organization-wide blast radius of a dependency change.
ventures.role: Designed the product, graph model, algorithms, and senior-engineer audit.
ventures.system: PostgreSQL for identity and history, Neo4j for dependency traversal, and task-aware model routing across hosted and local models.
ventures.state: Working multi-tenant product with more than 200 tests.
ventures.lesson: AI-assisted engineering needs explicit dependency truth before it needs another generator.

ventures.name: Crucible
ventures.thesis: Engineering workflows that make agents show their work.
ventures.problem: An agent’s confident report is insufficient evidence that a change is correct, complete, or recoverable.
ventures.role: I turn engineering judgment into reusable agent workflows, adversarial review, and executable acceptance rules.
ventures.system: Structured agent reports, claim-level evidence checks, risk-based verification, mutation and undo evidence, concurrent review, and bounded revision loops.
ventures.state: Public toolkit with runtime hooks and regression tests. Separately, my internal agent-engineering work supports daily operations and was adopted and extended by QA, Operations, and upstream/downstream teams.
ventures.lesson: I separate model judgment from the code that checks evidence structure, enforces workflow decisions, and controls when work can proceed.
